answer: Admission locks one timber lot, worth 60 units, per identity in exclusive escrow for 8 epochs, returned after a clean exit, and a registry refuses any pledged lot. At pledge, verifiers ring a quartz inlay in the lot and record its resonant frequency as its fingerprint. Unannounced sparrow drones re-ring the quartz and match both against the registry; a fingerprint pledged to another identity is refused at entry, and a mismatch or missing lot forfeits the 60. One lot sits in one place, so sharing fails: 1,000 fakes need 1,000 lots and 60,000 locked, while an honest agent locks one lot once.
